issues: fin/core.py holds a single ~800-line Book class that mixes schema, storage plumbing, authorization, domain rules and every report, and the CLI calls the unbound method `Book.loan_schedule(None, ...)` (cli.py main) to avoid opening a database, which shows the class has no clean separation.

fin/core.py report_ledger sums the raw amounts of ACCOUNT and all its descendants without checking their currencies, so a parent with children in different currencies gives a mixed-currency running balance that it labels as ACCOUNT's currency.

fin/core.py money() silently rounds inputs such as '10.005' to cents instead of rejecting amounts with more than two decimals, so typos in posting, payment and import amounts are accepted without any warning.

fin/core.py Book.run catches nothing but UserError upstream, so a sqlite3.OperationalError (for example a locked or corrupted database during a command) gets past cli.main as a traceback instead of a clean exit 2; server.make_server's int(Content-Length) likewise crashes the handler on a malformed header.

fin/server.py _str accepts JSON numbers (including floats) for amounts and converts them with str(), so a client can send float money values like 0.1+0.2 artefacts into Decimal parsing, and handle() calls book.authorize twice (again inside book.run).

tests/test_core.py test_loan checks schedule totals with float sums and contains the tautological assertion `assertEqual(r[-1]['principal'], r[-1]['principal'])`; several tests also bundle many unrelated scenarios into one method, which makes failures harder to locate.
strengths: Every mutating command runs inside Book.run's BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, so failed imports, recurring runs and closed-period violations leave the database untouched, and the tests check this.
Money is stored as text and handled as Decimal throughout, with one fmt/r2 path that gives half-up rounding and never prints '-0.00'; all SQL values are passed as parameters.

The CLI uses a single table-driven HANDLERS dispatch and the HTTP API reuses the same Book methods and authorization (UserError subclasses carrying 400/401/403/404), so the JSON shapes and validation match across both interfaces.
